advertisements.title: One account states that the name Titay comes from the word “Taytay,” a Subanen…
advertisements.description:
One account states that the name Titay comes from the word “Taytay,” a Subanen and Visayan word meaning bridge.

One version of our history suggests that the Subanens and Kalibugans were among the original inhabitants of the area known as Taytay, referring to the bridges found along their homes and communities. Over time, the name evolved and came to be known as Titay.

Inspired by this story, the arch of Taytay Market takes the form of a bridge; a symbol of connection, heritage, and community.

Welcome to Taytay Market, a bridge that connects Titayanons. A place where our history meets the present, and where every Titayanon comes together.

**𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 ||** Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel promptly responded to a request for emergency medical assistance at Barangay Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, involving a male patient who sustained an ankle injury while playing basketball.

Upon arrival at the basketball court, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. The patient was found seated on a chair, conscious and oriented, complaining of pain and swelling in the affected ankle following a twisting injury.

Immediate first aid was provided by applying a cold pack for 15 minutes, securing the affected ankle with an elastic bandage, and elevating the injured extremity to help reduce swelling and discomfort. The patient's vital signs were assessed, and his condition was monitored following the initial assessment and first aid.

The patient remained in stable condition and was left at the scene after being advised to seek medical evaluation if the pain or swelling persisted, worsened, or if additional symptoms developed.

Titay MFS reminds the public, especially athletes and sports enthusiasts, to observe proper precautions during physical activities and seek appropriate medical attention when injuries occur.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: **0965-509-0944.**

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel promptly responded to a reported vehicular accident at Barangay Kitabog, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, involving a female patient who sustained abrasions to the right eyebrow and left toe.

Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. The patient was found seated on a chair at the roadside, conscious and oriented. Further assessment revealed abrasions on the right eyebrow and left toe.

Immediate first aid was provided by cleansing the affected areas with an appropriate wound-irrigation solution, followed by the application of povidone-iodine (Betadine) to help reduce the risk of infection. The patient's condition was assessed, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 15 recorded.

Medical transport to the nearest appropriate health facility was offered for further evaluation and treatment. However, the patient declined transport after being informed of the potential risks associated with refusing medical care. The Refusal of Transport waiver was explained, signed, and properly secured. The patient was left at the scene in stable condition and advised to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms persisted, worsened, or new symptoms developed.

Titay MFS reminds the public that even seemingly minor injuries following a vehicular accident may require medical evaluation. Prompt assessment and appropriate medical care are essential for ensuring safety and preventing possible complications.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. The patient was found seated on a chair at the roadside, conscious and oriented. Further assessment revealed multiple abrasions on both knees, the right elbow, the left fingers, and the right metacarpal region. Swelling was also noted over the right parietal region of the head.

Immediate first aid was provided by applying a cold compress to the affected area of the head to help alleviate swelling and discomfort. The abrasions were cleansed using an appropriate wound-irrigation solution, followed by the application of povidone-iodine (Betadine) to help reduce the risk of infection. 𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 ||Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel promptly responded to a reported vehicular accident at Barangay Namnama, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, involving a 65-year-old male patient who sustained multiple open fractures and severe bleeding in his left lower extremity.

Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team secured the area and immediately conducted a primary assessment. The patient was found lying supine on the ground, conscious and oriented. Further assessment revealed multiple open fractures involving the left femur, patella, and tibia-fibula, accompanied by significant bleeding and associated soft-tissue injuries.

Immediate emergency medical care was provided to control the bleeding and stabilize the patient. A tourniquet was applied to the proximal left thigh, while gauze and an elastic bandage were used to manage the bleeding.         Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. One female patient was found sitting on a chair at the roadside, conscious and oriented following a vehicular crash. Upon assessment, abrasion was noted on the right knee, tenderness on the left hip and abrasion on the left dorsal foot.

Ilayo ang apoy, spark, sigarilyo, at iba pang ignition sources sa flammable materials. Tiyaking ligtas ang lugar bago magsagawa ng welding, cutting, o grinding.

Tandaan: Isang simpleng pag-iingat ngayon ay maaaring makaiwas sa malaking sunog at pagkawala ng buhay at ari-arian. 💪🧯

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel received a report regarding a vehicular accident at Barangay Palomoc, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay.

Upon receipt of the report, the responding team immediately proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.

Upon arrival, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. An adult male patient was found unconscious and unresponsive following the vehicular crash. Initial assessment revealed signs consistent with blunt head trauma, including contusion and swelling around the left orbital area and an avulsion wound on the left frontal region.

Immediate first aid was rendered by applying direct pressure to the frontal wound to help control bleeding, followed by securing the dressing with an elastic bandage. High-flow oxygen was administered via a non-rebreather mask at 15 liters per minute. The patient's condition and vital signs were continuously monitored.

Vital signs were assessed and recorded as follows: BP 100/70 mmHg, PR 70 bpm, RR 20 cpm, SpO₂ 92%, and temperature 36.1°C, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5.

Due to the patient's critical condition, he was immediately transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for definitive medical evaluation and management.

Upon arrival at the medical facility, the patient was safely transferred and properly endorsed to the physician on duty for continuity of care.

newsArticles.summary:
BFP Titay Conducts Fire Square Roadshow for Titay District Student Leaders

TITAY, Zamboanga Sibugay — September 12, 2026 — More than just classroom lessons, fire safety education came alive as the Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) conducted a Fire Square Roadshow for student leaders of the Titay District at Titay National High School, Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The activity equipped young leaders with essential knowledge and practical skills in fire prevention, basic firefighting, rescue, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH), empowering them to become active advocates of safety and preparedness in their schools, homes, and communities.

The activity aimed to strengthen the knowledge, skills, and preparedness of student leaders in preventing and responding to fire and other emergencies. It provided participants with practical lessons and demonstrations on basic firefighting, rescue techniques, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH).

The Fire Square Roadshow emphasized the important role of students as fire safety advocates and responsible members of the community. By equipping young leaders with essential fire safety knowledge and emergency response skills, the BFP seeks to help build a culture of preparedness and strengthen community resilience.

At this magnitude, no damage and aftershocks are expected.

✅ Stay calm and avoid spreading unverified information.
✅ Familiarize yourself with safe evacuation areas and emergency exits.
✅ Prepare and maintain your emergency go bag.
✅ During strong earthquakes, remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
✅ Follow only official updates from PHIVOLCS and LDRRMO-Titay.
